title: Hypertension diagnosis on single visit (severe BP)
recommended_action: Diagnose hypertension without further repeat measurements

evidence.passage: The diagnosis might be made on a single visit, if BP is ≥160/100 mmHg or there is accompanying evidence of hypertension mediated organ damage (HMOD)

title: Hypertension diagnosis requiring repeat measurements (moderate BP)
recommended_action: Perform repeat BP measurements on three separate occasions within 1‑4 weeks before confirming diagnosis

evidence.passage: When the initial SBP is between 140 and 159 mmHg, or the DBP is between 90 and 99 mmHg, repeat measurements should be performed on three separate occasions within a period of 1 to 4 weeks to determine whether a diagnosis of hypertension is valid

title: Out‑of‑office blood pressure measurement
recommended_action: Confirm hypertension diagnosis using home blood pressure monitoring (HBPM) or ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) if available

evidence.passage: If possible and available, the diagnosis of hypertension should be confirmed by out‑of‑office BP measurement (i.e., HBPM and/or ABPM)

title: Follow‑up BP measurement frequency when hypertension not diagnosed
recommended_action: Measure clinic blood pressure at least every 3 years; measure more frequently if BP is close to 140/90 mmHg

evidence.passage: If hypertension is not diagnosed, measure the person's clinic blood pressure at least every 3 years subsequently, and consider measuring it more frequently if the person's clinic blood pressure is close to 140/90 mmHg

title: Blood pressure re‑measurement schedule based on office BP level

variants.action: Remeasure within 3 years (1 year in those with other risk factors)
Confirm with repeated office visits. If possible, confirm with out‑of‑office BP measurement
Confirm within a few days or weeks

evidence.passage: Remeasure within 3 years (1 year in those with other risk factors)

title: Assessment of postural hypotension
recommended_action: Patient should lie down for 5 minutes, then measure BP and pulse rate. After standing, repeat BP and pulse rate measurements at 1 and 3 minutes.

evidence.passage: PaƟent should lie down for 5 minutes, and measure BP and pulse rate. Then have the paƟent stand and repeat BP and pulse rate measurements 1 and 3 minutes aŌer standing.

title: Medication review for postural hypotension with ≥20 mmHg systolic drop on standing
recommended_action: Medication is to be reviewed; subsequent BP should be measured with the person standing and the patient may be referred to specialist care if symptoms persist.

evidence.passage: If the systolic BP falls by ≥ 20 mmHg when the person is standing, medicaƟon is to be reviewed, subsequent BP is to be measured with the person standing and the paƟent may be referred to specialist care if symptoms of postural hypotension persist.

title: Take comprehensive hypertension history
recommended_action: Obtain detailed medical, family, and lifestyle history to assess risk factors and possible secondary causes of hypertension

evidence.passage:
The key issues that need to be addressed in the history include:
Risk factors assessment:
    *  Family and personal history of hypertension, CVD, stroke, or renal disease.
    *  Family  and  personal   history   of   associated   risk   factors   (e.g.,   familial hypercholesterolaemia)
    *   Dietary history and salt intake
    *  Smoking history
    *  Alcohol consumpƟon
    *   History of physical exercise/sedentary lifestyle
    *   History of erecƟle dysfuncƟon

title: Take comprehensive hypertension history
recommended_action: Obtain detailed history including sleep history, prior hypertension in pregnancy/pre‑eclampsia, oral contraceptive use, symptoms of target‑organ damage (brain, heart, kidney, peripheral arteries), prior antihypertensive drug use and adherence

evidence.passage:
  Sleep history, snoring, sleep apnoea (information also from partner)
  Previous hypertension in pregnancy/pre‑eclampsia
  History of oral contraceptive use.
History of symptoms of HMOD, CVD, stroke, and renal disease
    For Brain and eyes: headache, vertigo, syncope, impaired vision, TIA, sensory or motor deficit, stroke, carotid revascularisation, cognitive impairment, dementia (in the elderly).
   Heart: chest pain, shortness of breath, oedema, myocardial infarction, coronary revascularisation, syncope, history of palpitations, arrhythmias (especially AF), heart failure
    Kidney: thirst, polyuria, nocturia, haematuria, urinary tract infections.
    Peripheral arteries: cold extremities, intermittent claudication, pain free walking distance, pain at rest, peripheral revascularisation, patient or family history of CKD (e.g., polycystic kidney disease).
History of Antihypertensive Drug Treatment
    Current/past antihypertensive medication including effectiveness, intolerance or side effects of previous medications.
   Adherence to therapy and in non‑compliant patients the reason behind it (including financial constraint).

title: Perform comprehensive physical examination for hypertension
recommended_action: Conduct physical exam including weight, height, BMI, waist circumference, neurological and cognitive assessment, fundoscopic exam for hypertensive retinopathy, cardiac and carotid auscultation, peripheral artery palpation, bilateral arm BP measurement, skin inspection for café‑au‑lait patches, and kidney palpation for enlargement

evidence.passage:
Physical Examination
The physical examination should include the following:
   Weight and height measured on a calibrated scale, with calculation of BMI
    Waist circumference
    Neurological examination and cognitive status
    Fundoscopic examination for hypertensive retinopathy
   Palpation and auscultation of heart and carotid arteries
   Palpation of peripheral arteries
   Comparison of BP in both arms (at least once)
    Skin inspection: cafe‑au‑lait patches of neurofibromatosis (phaeochromocytoma)
    Kidney palpation for signs of renal enlargement in polycystic kidney disease

title: Baseline investigations for all hypertensive patients
recommended_action: Obtain blood tests (sodium, potassium, serum creatinine, eGFR; lipid profile and fasting glucose if available), urine dipstick analysis, and a 12‑lead ECG

evidence.passage: All hypertensive paƟents should undergo a limited number of invesƟgaƟons, these include: • Blood test o Sodium, potassium, serum creaƟnine and esƟmated glomerular ﬁltraƟon rate, (eGFR) o If available lipid proﬁle and fasƟng glucose • Urine analysis: DipsƟck urine test • 12-lead ECG for detecƟon of atrial ﬁbrillaƟon, leŌ ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), ischemic heart disease.

title: Additional investigations for most hypertensive patients
recommended_action: Obtain haemoglobin/haematocrit, chest X‑ray, and echocardiogram as indicated

evidence.passage: For most paƟents: • Haemoglobin and/or haematocrit • Chest X-ray: to detect cardiomegaly, heart failure, coarctaƟon of the aorta • Echocardiogram: to detect or quanƟfy leŌ ventricular hypertrophy

title: Tests for assessment of hypertensive mediated organ damage (HMOD)
recommended_action: Perform urine albumin‑creatinine ratio, blood creatinine/eGFR, and fundoscopy to detect renal disease and hypertensive retinopathy (especially in grade 2 or 3 hypertension)

evidence.passage: Tests for assessment for HMOD • Urine albumin: creaƟnine raƟo: To detect elevaƟons in albumin excreƟon indicaƟve of possible renal disease. • Blood creaƟnine and eGFR: To detect possible renal disease. • Fundoscopy: To detect hypertensive reƟnopathy, especially in paƟents with grade 2 or 3 hypertension.

title: Echocardiography
recommended_action: Perform echocardiography to evaluate cardiac structure and function when this information will influence treatment decisions.

evidence.passage: Echocardiography: To evaluate cardiac structure and function when this information will influence treatment decisions.

title: Carotid ultrasound
recommended_action: Perform carotid ultrasound to determine the presence of carotid plaque or stenosis, particularly in patients with cerebrovascular disease or vascular disease elsewhere.

evidence.passage: Carotid ultrasound: To determine the presence of carotid plaque or stenosis, particularly in patients with cerebrovascular disease or vascular disease elsewhere.

title: Abdominal ultrasound and Doppler studies
recommended_action: Use abdominal ultrasound and Doppler studies to evaluate renal size and structure, exclude renal tract obstruction, assess abdominal aorta for aneurysm, examine adrenal glands for adenoma or pheochromocytoma, and screen renal arteries for renovascular disease, especially with asymmetric renal size.

evidence.passage:
Abdominal ultrasound and Doppler studies:
 i) To evaluate renal size and structure (e.g., scarring) and exclude renal tract obstruction as possible underlying causes of CKD and hypertension
 ii) Evaluate abdominal aorta for evidence of aneurysmal dilation and vascular disease.
 iii) Examine adrenal glands for evidence of adenoma or phaeochromocytoma (CT or MRI preferred).
 iv) Renal artery Doppler studies to screen for the presence of renovascular disease, especially in the presence of asymmetric renal size

title: Pulse Wave Velocity (PWV)
recommended_action: Measure pulse wave velocity as an index of aortic stiffness and underlying arteriosclerosis.

evidence.passage: Pulse Wave velocity (PWV): An index of aortic stiffness and underlying arteriosclerosis

title: Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI)
recommended_action: Screen with Ankle-Brachial Index to detect lower extremity artery disease (LEAD).

evidence.passage: Ankle Branchial Index (ABI) Screen for evidence of Lower Extremity Artery Disease (LEAD)

title: Cognitive function testing
recommended_action: Perform cognitive function testing to evaluate cognition in patients with symptoms suggestive of cognitive impairment.

evidence.passage: Cognitive function testing: To evaluate cognition in patients with symptoms suggestive of cognitive impairment.

title: Brain imaging
recommended_action: Obtain brain imaging to evaluate the presence of ischemic or hemorrhagic brain injury, especially in patients with a history of cerebrovascular disease or cognitive decline.

evidence.passage: Brain imaging: To evaluate the presence of ischemic or haemorrhagic brain injury, especially in patients with a history of cerebrovascular disease or cognitive decline.

title: Follow‑up blood pressure measurement schedule after initial reading

variants.action: Remeasure within 3 years (1 year if other risk factors)
Confirm with repeated office BP measures within 1‑4 weeks

evidence.passage: <130 and <85  Remeasure within 3 years (1 year in those with other risk factors)

title: Indications for specialist referral in hypertension
recommended_action: Refer patients with accelerated or malignant hypertension, suspected secondary hypertension, resistant hypertension, recent onset target organ damage, pregnancy, or children <18 years old to the appropriate specialist.

evidence.passage: Patients with the following conditions should be referred to the appropriate specialist for further assessment. Indications for referral to the appropriate specialist include: accelerated or malignant hypertension; suspected secondary hypertension; resistant hypertension; recent onset of target organ damage; pregnancy; children <18 years old.
